heroHeadline: Tarco and Sudanair Restore Khartoum Flights on Day 1121; RSF Masses Forces at Libya-Egypt-Sudan Border as Aviation Revenue Losses Top $1B
heroSubtitle: On Day 1121, Sudan's civilian aviation resumed at full multi-carrier capacity for the first time since the war began: Tarco Aviation and Sudanair joined Badr Airlines at Khartoum International Airport, completing a rapid ten-day recovery after the May 4–5 RSF/UAE drone attacks that forced a four-day closure. Sudan's Civil Aviation Authority simultaneously revealed that the war has cost Sudan over $1 billion in cumulative aviation revenue since April 2023 — covering three years of airport inactivity, canceled maintenance contracts, suspended international routes, and rerouted overflights. A separate MadaMasr intelligence report from May 8 disclosed that RSF forces are massing near the Sudan–Libya–Egypt border triangle in Sudan's far northwest, potentially opening a new strategic axis through Libyan territory via RSF-LNA networks — a second front distinct from the Ethiopia border confrontation dominating Sudan's diplomatic agenda. Also on May 8, an RSF drone struck the home of a SAF-affiliated military commander near Khartoum, killing 15 — the latest in RSF's campaign of targeted strikes on SAF-aligned personnel in the recaptured capital. Sudan's civil war now enters Day 1121 with 14 million displaced, an estimated 150,000+ killed, and 34 million in urgent humanitarian need — against a backdrop of no ceasefire framework, an 84%-underfunded UN humanitarian appeal, and escalating confrontation with both Ethiopia and the UAE.
